shadshiny

shadshiny brings the shadcn/ui design system to Shiny. It is a broad, experimental reimplementation: 76 accessible, themeable components rebuilt in framework-free CSS and vanilla JavaScript, then wrapped as ordinary R functions with native Shiny input bindings.

  • No build step, no npm, no React. Components are plain htmltools tags backed by a single bundled asset dependency.
  • Native Shiny inputs. Read values with input$id; drive them from the server with update_shad_*(). Modules, renderUI() and bookmarking all work.
  • Layout primitives. shad_container(), shad_stack() and shad_grid() cover page layout on the token spacing scale, and shad_page_sidebar() / shad_page_navbar() assemble a whole app shell in one call.
  • Full data table. shad_data_table() does multi-column sort, global and per-column filtering, paging, and selection that survives paging, all client-side and themed, with no DT. The experimental shad_data_table_server() adds lazy server-backed paging.
  • Dashboards & charts. shad_value_box() and shad_chart_container() for the shell; shad_sparkline() and shad_mini_donut() draw inline SVG that follows the theme in CSS with no re-render; shad_theme_ggplot2() / shad_theme_plotly() / shad_theme_echarts4r() restyle plots onto the live theme.
  • Server-side validation. shad_validator() plus a rule set drive aria-invalid and inline, shadcn-styled field messages.
  • Streaming chat. shad_chat_ui() / shad_chat_server() render a stick-to-bottom transcript from any token source, so an ellmer stream drops straight in.
  • Structured AI workbench (experimental). shad_chat_workbench_ui() / shad_chat_workbench_server() render provider-owned public text, source, tool, attachment, and status events without an AI SDK or network call.
  • Coexists with Bootstrap 5 / bslib. Dark mode keys off the same signals bslib::input_dark_mode() uses, so theme sync needs no glue.
  • OKLCH token theming. Seven presets out of the box, switchable at runtime, plus custom palettes via shad_theme() and the shadcn theme registry.

shadshiny is an independent reimplementation. It ships no shadcn/ui or Radix source, only visually-compatible CSS/JS written for this package. See Attribution.

API stability

The package remains experimental as a whole while its release-facing core is being stabilized across R versions and platforms. The stable core boundary for the current development line is the documented page, layout, input, overlay, theme, client-side data-table, validation, chat, and update_shad_*() APIs, including their tested Shiny value and lifecycle contracts.

The following remain experimental integration edges: importing themes from an external shadcn/tweakcn registry schema, optional chart adapters whose behavior also depends on third-party packages, live integrations with external chat stream providers, the server-backed/lazy data-table helper, the questionnaire workflow, and the ExtendedTask button lifecycle binding. These boundaries may change before a stable 1.0 release.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("orijitghosh/shadshiny")

Quick start 

library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)

ui <- page_shad(
  theme_preset = "violet",
  shad_card(
    shad_card_header(
      shad_card_title("Create account"),
      shad_card_description("Enter your details below.")
    ),
    shad_card_content(
      shad_input("email", label = "Email", type = "email",
                 placeholder = "you@example.com"),
      shad_select("plan", label = "Plan",
                  choices = c(Free = "free", Pro = "pro", Team = "team"),
                  selected = "pro"),
      shad_checkbox("tos", label = "I accept the terms")
    ),
    shad_card_footer(
      shad_button(inputId = "submit", "Sign up", variant = "default")
    )
  ),
  verbatimTextOutput("out")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$out <- renderPrint(
    list(email = input$email, plan = input$plan, tos = input$tos)
  )
  observeEvent(input$submit, {
    if (!isTRUE(input$tos)) {
      shad_toast_error("Please accept the terms.")
    } else {
      shad_toast_success(paste("Welcome,", input$email))
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Run the flagship demo, which covers every component:

shad_run_example("kitchen-sink")

Components

Names marked + have no shadcn/ui counterpart; they are shadshiny additions. The marker covers components only. The server-side API (update_shad_*(), shad_<name>_open() / _close(), shad_show_dialog(), the toast functions) is Shiny plumbing that shadcn/ui has no equivalent for by construction, so it goes unmarked throughout.

Every stateful component is namespaced-module safe and has a matching update_shad_*() server helper where it holds a value. Overlays add shad_<name>_open() / shad_<name>_close(). Inputs that take an initial value seed it from shiny::restoreInput(), so enableBookmarking() restores them on reload.

Data tables

shad_data_table() is an input, not an output. It serialises the frame once and does everything else in the browser, so interaction never round-trips to R unless you ask for it.

ui <- page_shad(
  shad_data_table(
    "tbl", sales,
    columns = list(
      amount = shad_col("Amount", format = shad_fmt_number(2, prefix = "$")),
      status = shad_col("Status", format = shad_fmt_badge(
        c(paid = "default", refunded = "destructive")
      ))
    ),
    selection = "multiple", filter = "both", page_size = 25
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # $selected, $sort, $filter, $page, $pageSize
  observe(print(input$tbl$selected))
}

Formatters keep the raw value as the sort key, so a $1,200.00 cell still sorts numerically. See vignette("data-tables").

Server-backed paging (experimental)

For datasets that should not be serialized into the browser, keep the constructor empty/loading and connect it to a source function:

ui <- page_shad(
  shad_data_table(
    "orders", data = NULL, selection = "multiple", filter = "both",
    page_size = 25, loading = TRUE
  )
)

server_rows <- data.frame(
  order_id = sprintf("order-%03d", seq_len(100L)),
  customer = paste("Customer", seq_len(100L)),
  status = rep(c("paid", "pending", "refunded"), length.out = 100L),
  amount = seq(12.50, by = 7.25, length.out = 100L),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

server_source <- function(request) {
  filtered <- server_rows
  global <- trimws(request$filter$global)
  if (nzchar(global)) {
    hit <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(filtered, function(x) {
      grepl(tolower(global), tolower(as.character(x)), fixed = TRUE)
    }))
    filtered <- filtered[hit, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  for (column in names(request$filter$columns)) {
    needle <- trimws(request$filter$columns[[column]])
    if (nzchar(needle) && column %in% names(filtered)) {
      keep <- grepl(tolower(needle), tolower(as.character(filtered[[column]])), fixed = TRUE)
      filtered <- filtered[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    }
  }
  for (spec in rev(request$sort)) {
    filtered <- filtered[order(
      filtered[[spec$column]],
      decreasing = identical(spec$direction, "desc"), method = "radix"
    ), , drop = FALSE]
  }
  total <- nrow(server_rows)
  filtered_total <- nrow(filtered)
  first <- (request$page - 1L) * request$page_size + 1L
  page <- if (first <= filtered_total) {
    filtered[seq.int(first, min(first + request$page_size - 1L, filtered_total)), , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    filtered[0, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  list(data = page, total_rows = total, filtered_rows = filtered_total)
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  shad_data_table_server(
    "orders",
    source = server_source,
    columns = list(
      order_id = shad_col("Order"),
      amount = shad_col("Amount", format = shad_fmt_number(2, prefix = "$")),
      status = shad_col("Status", format = shad_fmt_badge(
        c(paid = "default", pending = "secondary", refunded = "destructive")
      ))
    ),
    row_key = "order_id",
    session = session
  )
}

For a database source, keep the same response shape, allowlist sort columns before composing SQL, and bind every user value. For example, the query layer can use DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, sql, params = list(global, page_size, offset)); do not paste request filters or sort names directly into SQL.

source() receives validated 1-based paging, multi-sort, global filtering, and named column filters. It must return no more than the requested page and the two total counts. The helper reuses shad_col() formatting, ignores stale responses, and shows a fixed safe error with retry if the source fails. Provide a unique, non-missing row_key for selections that survive paging; the helper does not provide database adapters, editing, grouping, pivoting, aggregation, downloads, or spreadsheet behavior. See vignette("data-tables") for the full contract.

Questionnaire workflows (experimental)

shad_questionnaire() sequences native fieldsets for single-choice, multiple-choice, and text questions. It reports one bookmarkable value with active, named answers, explicit skipped question names, and complete. All questions remain mounted; inactive or conditionally hidden questions are hidden and inert, so preserved answers do not enter the keyboard order.

ui <- page_shad(
  shad_questionnaire(
    "onboarding",
    shad_question(
      "direction", "What should be built?",
      choices = c(data = "Server table", rtl = "RTL"),
      shortcuts = c(data = "1", rtl = "2")
    ),
    shad_question(
      "details", "Describe the table", type = "text",
      show_if = list(direction = "data")
    )
  )
)

Use named equality data for show_if; the browser evaluates no application code. update_shad_questionnaire() patches active state, answers, or named errors, and reset = TRUE clears the workflow. The generic binding is module-safe and uses shiny::restoreInput() for bookmark restoration. See vignette("questionnaire") for validation, branching, modules, and the full state contract.

Field composition

Use native fieldsets for related controls, keeping shad_form_field() as the single-control wrapper. shad_field_group() supports vertical, horizontal, and container-responsive layouts; the responsive form switches to two logical columns at a 36rem container width and mirrors correctly in RTL.

shad_fieldset(
  "Payment",
  description = "Use the billing address associated with this card.",
  shad_field_group(
    shad_form_field(shad_input("card_number"), label = "Card number"),
    shad_form_field(shad_input("card_name"), label = "Name on card"),
    orientation = "responsive"
  )
)

shad_fieldset(
  "Settings",
  variant = "label",
  shad_field_group(
    shad_form_field(shad_switch("notifications"), label = "Notifications"),
    shad_field_separator("Optional"),
    shad_form_field(shad_input("timezone"), label = "Time zone")
  )
)

The native fieldset/legend relationship remains available to assistive technology, while field descriptions and validator errors retain their existing aria-describedby and aria-invalid behavior. The constructors forward ordinary HTML attributes, so a choice-card or radio group can be placed inside the same composition primitives.

Page shells and layout

Directionality

Set the page direction with ordinary HTML attributes passed through page_shad(...); this preserves the existing function signature:

page_shad(dir = "rtl", lang = "ar", shad_p("واجهة عربية"))

Floating panels inherit the nearest direction and language even after they are ported to body. For content that may mix scripts, use the browser’s automatic direction detection on the content wrapper or table root:

shad_message(tags$span(dir = "auto", "שלום / English"))
shad_data_table("mixed", data, dir = "auto")

Named physical sides such as data-side = "right" remain explicit placement contracts; logical spacing, borders, alignment, and start/end controls mirror with the document direction.

Three primitives cover page layout, on the same spacing scale the components use internally (gap = 4 is var(--shad-space-4)):

shad_container(size = "lg",
  shad_stack(
    shad_grid(kpi_one, kpi_two, kpi_three, min_width = "14rem"),
    shad_card(...),
    gap = 6
  )
)

shad_grid() takes min_width for an auto-fit track list, or cols for an exact count, optionally per breakpoint, cols = c(base = 1, md = 2, lg = 4).

Two shells assemble a whole page, taking the page_shad() theming arguments:

ui <- shad_page_navbar(
  shad_tab("overview", "Overview", overview_ui),
  shad_tab("reports",  "Reports",  reports_ui),
  title = "Acme", inputId = "nav"
)

ui <- shad_page_sidebar(sidebar = shad_sidebar(...), title = "Acme", body_ui)

See vignette("layout").

Dialogs from the server

Overlays can be declared in the UI with a trigger, or built in the server when their content depends on what just happened:

observeEvent(input$delete, {
  shad_show_dialog(shad_dialog(
    "confirm", title = paste("Delete", input$project, "?"),
    description = "This cannot be undone.",
    footer = tagList(shad_dialog_close_button(),
                     shad_button(inputId = "go", "Delete", variant = "destructive"))
  ))
})

It opens itself and, by default, removes itself once it closes. Also takes shad_alert_dialog(), shad_sheet() and shad_drawer(). See vignette("overlays-and-server").

⌘K navigation 

shad_command_palette("palette", items = list(
  "Go to"   = c(Dashboard = "dashboard", Reports = "reports"),
  "Actions" = list(list(value = "new", label = "New report", shortcut = "N"))
))

observeEvent(input$palette_event, { ... })   # fires on every activation

Observe input$palette_event, not input$palette: Shiny drops a repeat of the same value, so picking “Reports” twice would only fire once.

Charts that follow the theme

Themes switch at runtime, which a plot rendered in R cannot see on its own. shad_current_theme() is the bridge: read it in a render block and the plot re-runs whenever the preset or dark mode changes.

output$plot <- renderPlot({
  shad_current_theme()
  ggplot(df, aes(month, revenue)) +
    geom_col(fill = shad_chart_colors(1)) +
    shad_theme_ggplot2()
})

shad_chart_colors() returns the categorical ramp as hex (OKLCH converted in base R, with no new dependency). shad_tokens() exposes the full token set as CSS strings.

For small inline graphics, skip the plotting stack. shad_sparkline() and shad_mini_donut() are inline SVG painted with the chart tokens, so a dark-mode toggle restyles them in CSS with no re-render and no round trip:

shad_value_box("1,204", "Sessions", delta = "-3.1%",
               sparkline = shad_sparkline(sessions, type = "area"))

See vignette("charts").

Validation 

v <- shad_validator()
v$add_rule("email", shad_rule_required(), label = "Email")
v$add_rule("email", shad_rule_email())
v$add_rule("pw", shad_rule_min_chars(8))
v$bind_submit("submit")   # disables the button until valid
v$bind_summary("errors")  # renders an error summary panel
v$enable()

Put shad_rule_required() first so an empty field reports Required. rather than a format complaint. See vignette("forms").

Streaming chat

The handler may return a complete string, a chunk-yielding function, or a coro generator, so an ellmer stream drops straight in.

shad_chat_server("chat", handler = function(user, history) {
  chat$stream(user)
})

See vignette("chat").

ExtendedTask buttons (experimental)

bind_shad_task_button() connects an application-owned shiny::ExtendedTask to an existing shad_button(). It observes only task$status(): while the task is running the button shows a spinner and is disabled; after success or error it is enabled again, with optional labels. The helper never invokes the task, calls task$result(), creates workers, or imports an asynchronous backend.

task <- shiny::ExtendedTask$new(function(value) {
  expensive_work(value)  # return a promise-compatible result
})

ui <- shad_button("Run", inputId = "run")
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  bind_shad_task_button(task, "run", label_success = "Complete",
                        label_error = "Try again", session = session)
  observeEvent(input$run, task$invoke(input$value), ignoreInit = TRUE)
}

Task creation and asynchronous execution remain application concerns. For example, an application can use optional mirai or promises::future_promise() backends when installed:

if (requireNamespace("mirai", quietly = TRUE)) {
  task <- shiny::ExtendedTask$new(function(value) {
    mirai::mirai(expensive_work(value), value = value)
  })
}

if (requireNamespace("promises", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE)) {
  task <- shiny::ExtendedTask$new(function(value) {
    promises::future_promise(expensive_work(value))
  })
}

These optional packages are not shadshiny dependencies. See vignette("server-api") for the lifecycle contract.

Theming

Colours are OKLCH --shad-* custom properties, so never hard-code hex. Pick a preset at page level or swap it live:

page_shad(theme_preset = "green")            # slate stone blue green rose violet orange

# server-side, e.g. from a shad_select + shad_switch toolbar
update_shad_theme(preset = input$preset, dark = input$dark)

Build a custom palette with shad_theme(), scope one to a subtree with shad_theme_scope(), or import tweakcn / shadcn registry JSON with shad_theme_from_registry().

Dark mode is driven by .dark / [data-bs-theme="dark"], so bslib::input_dark_mode() toggles shadshiny components with no extra wiring. See vignette("theming").

Example apps

Each is a real app, launchable with shad_run_example():

kitchen-sink Every component, variant and server round-trip
01-auth-onboarding Tabbed auth card, a 4-step wizard, and input-OTP 2FA
02-analytics-dashboard Admin console: live chart, date range, command palette, mutable team directory
03-support-chat Conversation list, stick-to-bottom transcript, composer with attachments
04-storefront Product page: carousel, variant pickers, add-to-cart sheet, reviews
05-settings-profile Vertical tabs, profile and notification forms, a live appearance panel
06-docs-reader Sidebar nav, ⌘K palette, resizable article/TOC split, prev/next paging
07-data-explorer shad_data_table() with value boxes and theme-following plots
08-llm-chat Streaming shad_chat_server(); swap the handler for ellmer to go live
09-app-shell shad_page_sidebar(), layout primitives, sparklines, a ⌘K palette that navigates, and server-built dialogs

shadshiny is inspired by and visually compatible with shadcn/ui (MIT) by shadcn, which itself builds on Radix UI primitives. No upstream source code is vendored.
